newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 16.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on Oct 16. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
President Suharto, speaking during a visit to the troubled territory of East Timor, said that religious diversity should be seen not as a potential for conflict but as a strength.

The 30-million strong Moslem organisation, Nahdlatul Ulama, has denied its members were involved in church burnings in East Java last week. Party chairman Abdurrahman Wahid had previously said he believed many of the rioters were NU members.
The Indonesian Retail Merchants Association said that it wants legislative protection from big-budget foreign retail chains which operate in Indonesia under franchise agreements.

The connection between Indonesian conglomerate Lippo Group and American President Bill Clinton's Democratic Party is becoming the main plank of Republican Bob Dole's election strategy. Dole's camp has criticised Clinton's Democratic Party for accepting campaign contibutions from Lippo.
Japanese investors in Indonesia were unlikely to revise their plans because of recent arguments between the two governments over Indonesia's national car policy.
